result.title: Causal Discovery Bench: Can LLMs Autonomously Conduct Effective Experiments?
result.summary: As large language model (LLM) agents get actively adopted for autonomous research, they must not only reason over existing evidence, but also design informative experiments, allocate resources, analyze sequential observations, and decide when to stop and make conclusions. Yet these capabilities remain poorly measured. We introduce Causal-Discovery-Bench (https://github.com/mshen1019/causal-discovery-bench), a verifiable sandbox with configurable structural equation models and resource constraints to evaluate sequential experimental design and causal discovery without domain-semantic cues. Across 3,802 episodes with 13 models from 5 vendors, we analyze agent behavior along 40 metrics in seven families. Agents' performance exhibits a four-level difficulty hierarchy spanning single-experiment design, sequential exploration of causal relationships, resource-aware experimentation balancing cost and statistical power, and autonomous resolution of conflicting evidence. We identify a substantial performance gap between causal inference from correctly curated evidence and navigating causal discovery through autonomous experimentation: Analyzing agents' action trajectories attributes 94.5% of their mistakes to experimental design rather than to inference, which is further consolidated with ablation studies. Relaxing resource constraints alone does not reliably resolve failures in sequential discovery. In contrast, basic statistical tools substantially improve performance across multiple model families, while advanced tools provide little additional benefit when models lack prerequisite lower-level capabilities.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Causal-Discovery-Bench，用可验证沙盒与结构化方程模型评测 LLM agent 在资源约束下设计实验、序列探索因果关系并自主停止的能力，并在 13 个模型、3,802 个 episode 上按七类 40 项指标分析行为。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽非视觉多模态工作，但其对证据获取、实验设计、停止决策与冲突证据消解的分解，可为 LVR 的 LOOK/STOP 收益—成本评估及因果作用诊断提供问题表述与评价线索，值得核查。
